## Example 4.5 {#ss4-example-4-5 .ar-lesson }

The sum of the first six terms of an arithmetic sequence is $45$ and the sum of the first twelve terms is $-18$. Find the first term and the common difference. Hence find the $10$th term in the sequence.

::: {.split .ar-equation-prompt .fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
::: {.column-block}
$$\frac{6}{2}(2a+5d)=45$$

:::
::: {.column-block}
$$\frac{12}{2}(2a+11d)=-18$$

:::

:::

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 22 · Example 4.5</p>

::: notes

Reveal the simultaneous equations only after students translate the two sums. Simplify to 2a+5d=15 and 2a+11d=−3. Subtract: 6d=−18 so d=−3, a=15. Then a_10=15+9(−3)=−12. A negative sum is possible even though the first term is positive. Keep the final answers in the working rather than revealing them with the initial equations.

:::
